summary: IDXX was the one held-name event and it resolved well: 8-K 2.02 filed 11-02 plus Benzinga results show Q3 EPS $4.01 vs $3.71, sales $1.214B vs $1.191B, FY26 EPS and sales guidance raised (EPS $14.96-$15.16 vs $14.82 est), stock +20.1% intraday and +21.6% on the close. The 10-30 flag (print one trading day out, premise stale) was right to raise, and BTIG suspending its Buy on 10-30 was a pre-print warning that did not matter. Rest of the book was quiet on named-company news: no 8-K 4.01, 4.02 or 5.02 on any held name, and no new filings on DPZ, FAST, KR, MSCI, MSM, VRSN or WMT (the WMT 8-K 8.01 from 10-23 has aged out unread; L2 open item closes by expiry, not by resolution). Macro tape was a Nasdaq/chip rout (Intel -29%, Nasdaq down over 700 points premarket) with Apple reporting after the close; held ETFs VOO and VTI fell 0.3-0.4%. BTC/USD fell 2.1% on the day with the Binance hack still the dominant thread; the news flow is containment (90% of losses replaced, withdrawals resuming in phases, next phase Tuesday), not a new failure.

broken_theses.why: Not broken on filings, but unresolved. A fiscal.ai item dated 10-30 says Domino's lowered its FY2026 US net store-opening target and full-year operating income growth outlook, citing franchisee profitability and international headwinds. The linked source is a Zacks Starbucks-vs-Domino's comparison piece, and filings_7d for DPZ is empty (no 8-K of any item), so the cut is unconfirmed. If it is the company's own guidance it would normally come with an 8-K 2.02 or 7.01, and none appears; it could be stale Q3 guidance (reported 10-13) restated by an aggregator. The PM held at 10.5% on the stock's +2.5% day and re-anchored the invalidation to about $285. Treat the guidance-cut clause as still open. The earlier securities class action (motion to dismiss denied) and DA Davidson PT cut to $382 remain the real overhang.

The thesis invalidation names 'an exchange failure or adverse regulatory action'. The inputs support the PM's judgment that it has not tripped: Binance replaced 90% of the $6.3B stolen from company funds, said it completed security upgrades, is resuming withdrawals by network (next phase Tuesday), 98% of users stayed per CZ, and the CFTC chair's comments (offer a federal registration option, 'very concerning' cyber incidents) are posture, not action. Residual risks: the Secret Service and FBI probe (North Korea attributed), crypto exchange stocks falling on the hack, and ETH ETFs posting record monthly outflows. The price stop (about $75.3k) is the live test: the position is -8.4% against cost and BTC fell 2.1% today.

Thesis intact, clause live. Estimated earnings 11-05 (3 trading days; the file's date is last year plus 364 days and is not company-confirmed in this input, though the 10-30 review had a company confirmation). No filings or CARG headlines. The position is up 5.0% today and 7.6% on cost, so a miss would give back gains. The 'negative surprise inside five trading days' clause stays active through the print.
